target_customer: Internet service providers and telecom operators, from regional fiber and wireless ISPs to larger cable groups
problem: ISPs run on legacy OSS and BSS stacks of separate billing, provisioning, inventory and field tools. gaiia replaces them with one operating system.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for OSS/BSS software, with migration services
product_category: Telecom OSS/BSS operating system for ISPs

founders.name: Marc-Andre Campagna
previous_startups: Oxio (Canadian ISP, acquired by Cogeco in 2023)
founders.background_notes: Backgrounds not on the YC page; Oxio link comes from trade press saying gaiia began inside Oxio

founders.name: Francis Careau
founders.background_notes: Backgrounds not on the YC page; Oxio link inferred from press on the team behind Oxio

technical_complexity.rationale: A unified billing, provisioning, inventory and workflow platform with integrations to network vendors is large but standard enterprise software, with migration and telecom integrations as the hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: ISP back office systems are deeply integrated with billing and network gear, so migrations are costly and customers stay; the company claims 3x revenue growth for three years.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established ISP billing vendors kept serving their customers; none copied or bought gaiia. The company has stayed independent through 2026.

market_need_then: ISPs depended on legacy OSS and BSS and cobbled-together tools; a 2021 figure cited by Splynx counts about 2,800 US fixed wireless ISPs serving 6.9 million users.

identity.logo: Lowercase wordmark; no further description found
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and playful, e.g. 'If your BSS is kind of BS, talk to us' and 'grow better with gaiia'

branding.brand_signature: Lowercase name and cheeky lines that cast unhappy customers as Kryptonite
branding.community_and_virality: Trade press and case studies (LilaConnect, Resound); no fan or meme evidence

brand_strength.rationale: A playful voice stands out in dull enterprise software and trade press coverage is steady, but the spelling with a double i invites confusion with Gaia and Gaiam brands.

outcome_analysis: gaiia grew out of Canadian ISP Oxio, raised a 13M seed in October 2023, an 18M CAD Series A in June 2024 and a 40M Series B in May 2026, and now claims over 40 ISP customers and three years of more than 3x revenue growth. Founder domain knowledge and sticky back office software explain the strong trajectory.
notes: The YC page lists the batch as Winter 2021 but founded 2023; the batch label and the 2023 founding conflict, so founded_year is null (one summary says gaiia started inside Oxio before it was a standalone business). Founder names come from the YC page; their Oxio ties come from trade press summaries and are unverified. Total raised: Series B release says 66M USD, BetaKit says nearly 90M CAD, consistent after conversion. Competitor search returned only 2024 to 2026 vendor pages with no dated 2021 launches, so the competitor list is left empty as of founding; Powercode, Sonar, Azotel and Splynx exist as current alternatives. Marked complete because the Series B release states total funding.
